name: Preiss Route

pitch_detail.notes: From the large ledge near the waterfall streaks, climb about 80 ft up the obvious stair-stepped rock gully to a crack anchor.
Exit the gully slightly right, then a full pitch of fun slabby rock with a few good cracks and pockets for solid gear. Belay on a shelf with a couple of small pools and good belay cracks.
Angle left and up on easier rock to the base of the great slabs.
600-700 ft of sub-par, essentially unprotectable slab. Aim for the small, thick stubby tree on the upper rightish side of the face, then continue to the next small tree patch to belay.
Straight up more slabby rock to the large ledge under the steeper headwall — a great bivy ledge.
Traverse the big ledge to its left side and climb a fun blocky corner that ends at a small sandy notch.
A few difficult moves off the notch protected by a solid thin crack; the angle then relents to class 3 with small trees.
The last obstacle: a rock wall of about half a pitch on good rock with good protection.
Walk down and left through a small gap in the trees onto the gentle northern slope, hike around right and scramble the short back side of the sub-summit rock (4,804 ft).

rappels: No fixed rappel line on the route. Descend over the main West Peak summit and down the west ridge, or - if you have carried two 60 m ropes - rappel Infinite Bliss instead: counts for this rappel line differ - about 20 to 25 double-rope rappels. Do not head straight down the northwest backside slope.
descent_text: From the sub-summit, walk down and left through the small gap in the trees onto the gentle northern slope, then go up and over the main West Peak summit and descend the west ridge. Do NOT head straight down the northwest backside slope — the first ascensionist flags this specifically. The alternative, if you have carried two 60 m ropes, is to rappel Infinite Bliss (about 20 rappels off the chain stations); a single 70 m or 80 m is not long enough for those stations. Either way this is a long descent on brushy, disorienting terrain and should be started with hours of daylight in hand.
approach: Hike basically straight up, taking a line of least resistance for roughly 1,500 ft while staying left of the lower rocky slabs, with up to 3rd-class scrambling. A 20 ft dirty downclimb leads to the base of the first pitch.
overview: A 13-pitch, Grade IV trad line up a sub-summit rock near Garfield's West Peak, established solo in 1999.
beta: Moderate trad climbing up to 5.9 with good protection on most pitches; the crux-adjacent middle slabs are serious (R/X-rated) with real rockfall/fall exposure.
fa: Mike Preiss, solo/self-belayed, July 1999 (exact date within 7/20-22 1999 not settled)
face: The great slabs on the south side of the West Peaks (tops out on the 4,804 ft sub-summit)
